newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh hasina on Sunday said a vested quarter was carryiong out "sabotage" to disrupt normal public life.
Bangladesh and India will discuss a permanent arrangement for the sharing waters of the river Teesta at a meeting of the Joint River Commission due in the first week of April.
The Malaysian government will legalise 150,000 Bangladeshi workers by May, official sources in Dhaka said.
Commonwealth Secretary General Emeka Anyaku will arrive Bangladesh on March 20 on a three-day visit.
Dhaka University authorities on Sunday decided to restrict movements of outsiders in the campus area to stop further escalation of violence.
Energy Minister M Nooruddin Khan has requested the garment manufacturers to keep close their factories between 6-30 pm and 10-30 pm until the power situation improves.
A recent study on urban poverty found nearly 61 percent of people in towns and cities live below poverty line.
State Minister for Jute and Textile A K Fayezul Huq on Sunday said jute was facing severe competition from synthetic substitutes. REUTER
